question: Why are positive pairs so important in contrastive learning?
direct_answer: They define what the model should treat as the same underlying example.
expanded_answer: Positive pairs provide the training signal for invariance. If two augmented views or paired modalities come from the same underlying instance, the model is encouraged to map them nearby in embedding space. Without a clear positive-pair definition, the method would not know what structure to preserve, so the representation would not learn the intended semantic similarity.
key_points: They come from the same underlying sample or match
common_wrong_ideas: Positives are just extra data points
Any random pair can be positive
The model learns without specifying what counts as a match
